audit.whatIsWrong: Difficulty read 4/10 flat, which describes only the pre-6 lane.
audit.why: The lane is genuinely favoured to level 5 and genuinely lost after two items — a single low number hides the flip that decides most games.
audit.corrected: diffRating 4/10 to 5.5/10, with the difficulty and final-rating lines reworded to say early-favoured, late-losing.

audit.whatIsWrong: Level chart read Ornn for six of seven rows and never showed the level-6 flip.
audit.why: Packet levelChart is Skill, Ornn, Skill, Skill, Kassadin, Kassadin, Kassadin, and the page's own whys[5] and whys[6] already describe Kassadin taking the lane over — the chart contradicted its own text.
audit.corrected: Rows 0, 2, 3, 4, 5 and 6 flipped in matched full/content pairs to Skill, Skill, Skill, Kassadin, Kassadin, Kassadin; ratings moved to match.

audit.whatIsWrong: The page calls Null Sphere a silence in five places, and never gives Riftwalk's cooldown.
audit.why: Riot's text for Null Sphere is damage, channel-interrupt and a magic-damage shield — no silence. Void Stone reduces magic damage, which is what actually blunts Bellows Breath. Riftwalk is a 500-range blink at 5/3.5/2s, and Nether Blade (7s) is an auto-attack reset — the wind-up is the burst tell, not the cast.
audit.corrected: Silence claims replaced with the shield plus Void Stone interaction; Riftwalk's 5/3.5/2s and 500 range and the Nether Blade reset tell written into the phases, mid and spikes text.

audit.whatIsWrong: missingInteractions claims Bellows Breath cancels Null Sphere as a channel.
audit.why: The kit's 'channel' flag is a tooltip-parsing misfire: Riot's text says Null Sphere interrupts channels, it is not itself one. I did not write that claim to the page.
audit.corrected: No edit made; recorded in notes.

edits.before: Q-poke and AA-trade — your base stats are quietly elite. Identify how Kassadin contests the first waves before you commit anything.
edits.after: Q-poke and AA-trade — your base stats are quietly elite, but Kassadin is equally helpless at 1. Nobody wins; farm for levels.

edits.before: Full kit online — your core pattern starts now. Keep the wave near your side so Kassadin must walk into your engage range.
edits.after: Full kit online, but Null Sphere's shield absorbs magic damage and Void Stone cuts it further — trade with autos and the knock-up.

edits.before: The lane-control window: trade around Riftwalk's cooldown and bank small leads. If ahead, freeze and deny; if behind, farm safe.
edits.after: Your last free window before 6: E into your own pillar for the knock-up, and bank every plate you can before Riftwalk exists.

edits.before: Call of the Forge God re-engages a whole fight — and your forge prints item leads. Reassess every all-in at 6 — Kassadin's ultimate changes the math too.
edits.after: Riftwalk lands: a 500-range blink on 5s that walks out of your E-Q. Your R still catches him, but the lane stops being free at this level.

edits.before: Iceborn Gauntlet is your spike — force fights the moment it completes, on Riftwalk's cooldown.
edits.after: Rod of Ages outraces Iceborn Gauntlet — Riftwalk is 3.5s now and he stops standing still for your E.

edits.before: Two items on: your side-lane pattern is at full power. Kassadin carry threat 9.5/10 — close before the map decides instead of you.
edits.after: Kassadin carry threat 9.5/10: at 2s Riftwalk he kites you outright. Close the game before the side lane belongs to him.

edits.before: His mobility spike at 6. Kill him before it scales. Only engage once it is down or baited.
edits.after: A 500-range blink, 5s at rank 1 down to 2s at rank 3. Kill him before it scales past you.

edits.before: Your level-3 Bellows Breath gives unstoppable percent-HP poke and a shield he can't trade into, but his Q silence keeps it even.
edits.after: Bellows Breath gives percent-HP poke and a shield, but Null Sphere's magic shield eats it and Nether Blade out-trades you back.

edits.before: You can land E into your Q pillar for a knock-up, but he can farm safely behind his Q silence and magic shield — it's a skill check.
edits.after: You can land E into your Q pillar for a knock-up, but he farms safely behind Null Sphere's shield and Void Stone's magic reduction.

edits.before: Post-Rod-of-Ages Kassadin Riftwalks in, silences with Q and bursts you while his passive shield eats your W magic damage.
edits.after: Post-Rod-of-Ages Kassadin Riftwalks in every 2s, resets Nether Blade, and bursts you while Void Stone blunts your W damage.

edits.before: Farm safely behind his Q silence and magic shield until Rod of Ages / Tear come online
edits.after: Farm safely behind Null Sphere's shield and Void Stone until Rod of Ages / Tear come online

edits.before: Kassadin is melee-helpless at Levels 1-2 just like you are, so neither of you wins the opening — you both just farm. The lane turns at Level 3: once you have Q and W, your Bellows Breath gives you unstoppable percent-HP poke and a shield, and he has no blink yet to answer it. Don't waste E chasing — he has nothing to punish you, so just shove and chip him with W. His only early tool is the Q silence, which he uses defensively to peel a trade, not to win one.
edits.after: Kassadin is melee-helpless at Levels 1-2 just like you are, so neither of you wins the opening — you both just farm. The lane turns at Level 3: once you have Q and W, Bellows Breath gives percent-HP poke and a shield, and he has no blink yet to answer it. Don't waste E chasing — he has nothing to punish you, so shove and chip him with W. Null Sphere is a damage-and-shield tool, not a silence: it blunts your magic damage, so trade with autos and the E knock-up.

edits.before: Levels 4-5 are your real window — your E into your own Q pillar knock-up lands clean because he still has no Riftwalk to dash out of it, so punish any time he steps up to last-hit. Crash the wave and look to roam, because everything inverts at 6: the moment he hits Riftwalk (R) he blinks over your telegraphed E-Q and stops dying to ganks. Get your lead in before that, because his Q silence also shuts off your W mid-combo.
edits.after: Levels 4-5 are your real window — your E into your own Q pillar knock-up lands clean because he still has no Riftwalk to dash out of it, so punish any time he steps up to last-hit. Watch the Nether Blade wind-up: that auto reset is his burst tell, so step back on the animation, not the cast. Crash and roam, because everything inverts at 6 — Riftwalk is a 500-range blink on 5s, and 2s by rank 3.

edits.before: Once Kassadin has Rod of Ages and a couple items he owns this lane and the map — he Riftwalks in, silences you with Q to lock out your W shield, and bursts you while his passive magic shield blunts your only ranged damage. Your job was to make 6+ irrelevant; if you got ahead, hard-shove and group so his single-target threat means less, and let your team body him in a fight where your free Masterwork upgrades and CC chain still win. Do not try to 1v1 a fed Kassadin — he untargets and kites you to death.
edits.after: Once Kassadin has Rod of Ages and a couple of items he owns this lane and the map — he Riftwalks in from 500 range, resets Nether Blade, and bursts you while Void Stone's magic reduction and Null Sphere's shield blunt your only ranged damage. Your job was to make 6+ irrelevant; if you got ahead, hard-shove and group so his single-target threat means less, and let your team body him in a fight where your free Masterwork upgrades and CC chain still win. Do not try to 1v1 a fed Kassadin — he blinks and kites you to death.

notes: The kit file's 'channel: interruptible' flag on Null Sphere is a tooltip-parsing misfire — Riot's text says the ability interrupts channels, it is not one — so I did NOT write the missingInteractions line claiming Bellows Breath cancels it. Null Sphere also has not silenced since its rework; the page repeated 'Q silence' five times and that is now removed. Mirror kassadin__ornn records a 72.73% Kassadin win rate over only 22 games against this packet's 1248-game 55.05% for Ornn; I followed the packet chart, which agrees with the mirror's late-game conclusion anyway.
